mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS monthly change > 10,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE changes and SPX 20-day returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided catalog) would drive this hypothesis, but since we lack a proxy, we instead use HOUST (housing starts) as a leading indicator. Rising housing starts in the prior 2 months predict a reduction in policy uncertainty and improved business sentiment, producing negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above the 12-month moving average
failure_condition: HOUST growth is not predictive of negative SPX 5-day returns (p > 0.10 in Granger causality test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeding 2% suggests supply-side expansion that outpaces demand, causing equity valuation compression and negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth rate > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO acceleration is not associated with negative SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) shows a monthly acceleration above 0.3% for three months, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations that the Fed is likely to counter with rate hikes, which depresses equity forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change accelerates above 0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite CPIAUCSL acceleration (p < 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% suggests a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations, which can lead to higher inflation and a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between UNRATE and SPX 60-day returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail employment (PAYEMS) and a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) create a strong labor demand signal that, if sustained, elevates equity risk premia and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5,000 for two months while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points over the same period
failure_condition: The interaction of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes is not predictive of SPX 20-day returns (R-squared < 0.02).

mechanism_narrative: In a deflationary regime characterized by falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and persistently low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be positive due to reduced discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: regime: CPIAUCSL decreasing for 4 months and FEDFUNDS < 4%
failure_condition: During the specified regime, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
